# Cast pipeline

How pixels and sound get from the laptop to each TV, the patches that make it
work, and the measurements behind each choice. Both TVs share one video source.

## Video source: patched wf-recorder (zero-copy)

```
Hyprland (renders on AMD) ─wlr-screencopy─► LINEAR DMA-BUF allocated on the Intel iGPU
  ─► Intel VA-API: pad (RGB) → convert to NV12 → h264_vaapi ─► H.264 Annex-B on stdout
```

- **Capture:** `wlr-screencopy` straight from Hyprland, no portal or PipeWire.
  The buffer is allocated LINEAR on the Intel GPU; Hyprland (AMD, GCN 1.0)
  renders into it. All casting processes together use about 20% of one core
  (the old portal + GStreamer CPU path used about 350%).
- **Cross-GPU fixes** (wf-recorder patch, env vars):
  - `WF_FORCE_DMABUF=1` keeps DMA-BUF when the encoder GPU differs from the
    compositor GPU (stock wf-recorder disables it).
  - `WF_IMPLICIT_MODIFIER=1` advertises `DRM_FORMAT_MOD_INVALID` instead of
    LINEAR: GCN 1.0 amdgpu only lists implicit modifiers, so Hyprland rejected
    the explicit LINEAR pair ("format + modifier pair is not supported") and
    frames came out black.
  - `WF_ALLOC_DEVICE` allocates on another GPU (tested; no gain).
- **Frame rate:** `-B <fps>` passes the real frame rate to the encoder and
  caps capture to it. Without it the VA-API rate control assumed ~65535 fps
  (time base 1/1000000), budgeted ~183 bits per frame, and the i965 driver
  logged "Unrepairable underflow" (blocky video, text sharpening only on
  keyframes).
- **Steady frames:** `-D` captures every compositor frame (capped at `-B`)
  instead of damage-only. Both the Apple TV and the Chromecast show a frame
  only when the next one arrives; damage-only frames made the latency test read
  1.6–2.2 s, steady frames 0.67 s.
- **Robustness:** a null-bo guard (skip a slot with no DMA-BUF), and
  `WF_MAX_FAILURES` with backoff so window or fullscreen transitions do not
  kill capture. A display mode or scale change still fails; the cast restarts.
- **Encoder settings:** VBR at the target bitrate, peaks 2x, 1 s buffer, `bf=0`,
  `aud=1`, `async_depth=1`. Padding happens in RGB before NV12 conversion
  (padding in NV12 fills the bars with zero YUV, which is green).

**Where the capture CPU goes (profiled 2026-09-26):** mostly inside the i965 driver building
VME motion-search batches on the CPU per frame (`gen7_vme_walker_fill_vme_batchbuffer`); Haswell
has no low-power encoder and its quality levels (0–2) make no difference, so cost scales with
pixels, which is why 1080p/720p casts are ~3× cheaper than 1440p. The pad pass was a no-op
full-frame copy on the TV desktop (output = canvas): skipped with `DOUBLETAKE_NO_PAD=1` and in
`wf-capture.sh` (8% → 6% CPU, 141 → 173 frames per 10 s). H.264 stays: it is the only hardware
encode on Haswell and both receivers take it.

## AirPlay to the Office TV (doubletake)

Launcher: `cast-tv.sh` (under `cast-guard.sh`, restarts on exit code 1), started by
`raytube-cast start` as the unit `raytube-cast` with `CPUWeight=1000`.

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `DOUBLETAKE_WF_RECORDER` | patched wf-recorder | use the zero-copy capture instead of portal + GStreamer |
| `-hwaccel intel` | ffmpeg `h264_vaapi` on renderD129 | GStreamer's va plugin cannot encode on i965 |
| `DOUBLETAKE_CANVAS` | per-TV size, default 1920x1080, in both modes (720p / 1080p / 1440p) | Apple TV asks for 1280x720@30; bigger pictures are held behind the sound (see sync below). Mirror mode fits and pads the laptop screen into it; the TV desktop is created at exactly this size |
| `-fps` / `-bitrate` | 30 / 20000 | readable text; bandwidth is plentiful |
| `-target-latency-ms` | 110 | frames leave ~80 ms after capture; below ~75 ms of slack the Apple TV grows its buffer |
| `DOUBLETAKE_WF_ARGS` | `-D` (+ `-o TV` for the TV desktop) | steady frames; capture the TV output |
| `DOUBLETAKE_PULSE_PROPS` | `buffer-time=60000 latency-time=20000` (+ `device=raytube_tv.monitor`) | 10 ms chunks forced a 5 ms PipeWire quantum and xrun crackle; 200 ms default made audio stale |
| `DOUBLETAKE_NO_PAD` | `1` in desktop mode | the TV output already is the canvas size, so the pad pass is a no-op copy |
| `DOUBLETAKE_AUDIO_DELAY_MS` / `_FILE` | the TV's `~/.config/raytube/av-delay/<ip>` (Office TV 50 ms) | shift sound later to match the video stamp; the file is re-read every 500 ms |

doubletake patch also adds: `DOUBLETAKE_NO_COMPOSITOR`, `DOUBLETAKE_PW_PROPS`,
`DOUBLETAKE_NO_VAPOSTPROC`, `DOUBLETAKE_GL_CONVERT` (legacy portal path), and
audio that stays late for 3 s restarts the audio capture (see Stuck audio below).
Timing uses PTP; UFW must allow UDP 319/320 from the Apple TV.


**doubletake CPU:** start-code scanning (`findStartCode`) now jumps between `0x01` bytes with
`bytes.IndexByte` (0.92 → 0.12 ms per 1440p frame, identical to the old scan on 1M random inputs,
`startcode_test.go`); the rest is required chacha20-poly1305 encryption (AVX2) and ALAC packing.

**Stuck audio (2026-09-26):** when captured audio stays later than the target delay for
3 s (the sound server can get stuck holding a bigger buffer, e.g. under CPU starvation),
doubletake now **restarts only the audio capture** and the picture keeps playing. A third
stall within a minute still fails the stream, and `cast-tv.sh` restarts everything.
**Audio glitches (xruns):** PipeWire's default 512-sample cycle (10.7 ms) dropped audio under load
(Firefox video + background tools). `raytube-cast start` forces a 1024-sample cycle
(`pw-metadata -n settings 0 clock.force-quantum 1024`, cleared on stop); in a test that took
xruns from one every 20–30 s to none. `cast-watch.sh` also reads the capture stream's xrun counter
(pw-top ERR) every 5 s; more than 2 in 30 s raises the cycle to 2048 and notifies.
**Recovery: re-sync.** After glitches (or an audio-only capture restart) the Apple TV stays out
of sync and never catches up by itself. The protocol's way back (RTSP FLUSH + re-anchor via a
first-bit sync packet or SETRATEANCHORTIME, per the unofficial spec, shairport-sync and
airplay-esp32) isn't implemented in doubletake, but a fresh session always starts in sync, so
`raytube-cast resync` restarts the session (~5 s black). `cast-watch.sh` does this automatically once
things are calm for 10 s after a glitch burst or audio restart (at most every 5 min); also the
Display menu **Re-sync TV** button and TV mode **A**. Cast units run with `CPUWeight=1000` so the
audio path wins CPU contention (glitches at 00:07 on 09-27 coincided with load 9 from MCP servers).
**Headphones and TV sound (2026-09-27):** connecting AirPods moved the TV-desktop cast's audio
capture (targeted at `raytube_tv.monitor`) onto the AirPods' monitor, so the TV played everything the
AirPods did. `cast-watch.sh` now moves it back within 5 s in desktop mode (tested). `raytube-cast
tv-sound off` mutes just the capture stream, so the TV goes quiet while the laptop keeps playing.
`cast-watch.sh` (unit `raytube-watch`) logs every such event to
`~/.local/state/raytube/cast-watch.log` with CPU temperature, Hyprland CPU, load, the top
processes and the default sink at that moment.

**Audio/video sync (2026-09-26): send the size the TV asks for.** The Apple TV's `/info`
display asks for **1280x720, maxFPS 30**. Sending it 2560x1440 (TV desktop) made it hold the
picture ~0.9 s behind the sound, even though our timestamps, clock (±4 ms vs PTP) and packet
layout were correct (checked against UxPlay, pyatv, shairport-sync and the nto.github.io spec).
At 1280x720 it syncs by itself with **no audio delay**, and the cast costs a quarter of the CPU
(capture 6%, doubletake 5%); 1080p was also tested in sync (~50 ms audio lead = the post-encode
video stamp, so the Office TV delay is 50 ms). **Picture size is selectable per TV**:
Display menu → CAST → 720p | 1080p | 1440p (default 1080p), or `raytube-cast size <ip> 720p`,
stored in `~/.config/raytube/airplay-size/<ip>` and used in **both** modes (mirror mode fits and
pads the laptop screen into it; the old 3200x1800 canvas is gone). Changing it restarts the cast.
1440p is sharper but the TV holds the picture back. The per-TV audio delay (`raytube-cast av-delay`,
Display menu → Sound sync −/+ in 50 ms steps, `DOUBLETAKE_AUDIO_DELAY_FILE` re-read live) is only
for fine-tuning; the Office TV is set to 50 ms, which matches the ~50 ms audio lead at 1080p.
Screen (mirror) mode at 1080p has not been checked for sync yet (T-33).

## Cast Streaming to the Chromecast (omacast)

Launcher: `cast-chromecast.sh` (under `cast-guard.sh`, unit `raytube-cast`, `CPUWeight=1000`)
starts a fresh `omacastd`, then `omacast start --to "Chromecast HD"`. Chromecast casts always
use 1920x1080 (the TV desktop is created at that size, and `wf-capture.sh` then skips the scale
and pad passes).
Config: `~/.config/omacast/config.toml` (1080p30, 8000 kbps, audio on,
`video_command = wf-capture.sh {width} {height} {fps} {kbps}`).

omacast is a Rust Cast Streaming sender (mirroring app `0F5096E8`, H.264 +
Opus, AES-CTR frames, RTCP). It had never met real hardware; our patch fixes:

| Fix | Symptom it fixed |
|---|---|
| Sender Report sent **before** frame 0 | receiver drops packets that arrive before any SR, so the opening key frame never completed |
| Ignore checkpoints newer than the newest frame sent | the receiver's startup checkpoint (leader, `0xFF`) wiped every buffered frame |
| In-flight window 12 → 60 frames | ~16 frames shed at startup (first ACK takes ~0.5 s) |
| Discovery skips IPv6 link-local and never lets IPv6 replace IPv4 | intermittent `connecting to [fe80::…]:8009: Invalid argument` |
| **SSRCs in openscreen ranges** (audio 1–50000, video 50001–100000) | random SSRCs ≥ 2^31 got `Invalid or missing codec on first OFFER` in ~half of sessions |
| `receiverRtcpEventLog` off by default (`OMACAST_RTCP_EVENT_LOG=1` enables) | firmware rejects OFFERs requesting it |
| `video_command` config (external H.264 source) | reuse our zero-copy capture |
| `OMACAST_AUDIO_MONITOR` | TV desktop audio only |
| Receiver telemetry (INFO every 5 s) | self-check without watching the TV |
| `OMACAST_SETTLE_MS` / `OMACAST_OFFER_ATTEMPTS` | tunable OFFER retry (defaults 300 ms / 4) |

**Telemetry** lines in `~/.local/state/omacast/omacastd.log`:
`receiver: … checkpoints N, nacks N, keyframe requests N` per 5 s window, and
`receiver audio: checkpoints N`. Checkpoints ÷ 5 ≈ fps received complete;
keyframe requests mean decoder trouble; NACKs are Wi-Fi loss being repaired.
A 2-minute soak averaged 24.5 fps, 0 keyframe requests, audio ~53/s.

## Latency

Measured with `latency-test.html` (reaction time subtracted):

| Setup | Delay |
|---|---|
| Damage-only frames (both TVs) | 1.6–2.2 s |
| Steady frames (`-D`), Chromecast | ~0.67 s |

Frames leave the laptop ~80 ms after capture; PTP clock mapping to the Apple
TV is accurate to under 1 ms (verified by capturing its Follow_Up packets).
The rest is the receiver and the TV panel. TV Game Mode is the next cheap win.

## Dead ends (don't retry)

- AMD VCE encoding (`vah264enc`): crashed the GPU and display.
- Portal + PipeWire capture: xdph 1.4.1 "Out of buffers" permanent-freeze
  loop (fixed upstream in #424/#425, not installed); `pipewiresrc` needs
  `min-buffers=8`; the forced-live GStreamer `compositor` repeats stale frames.
- CPU colour conversion (GStreamer `videoconvert`, ffmpeg swscale): 130–290%
  of a core at 2880x1800. GL shader conversion on AMD is cheaper (31%) but the
  zero-copy path needs no conversion on the CPU at all.
- 4K canvas on this machine: CPU-bound, ~1 fps under load.
- 60 fps capture: Hyprland copy cost doubles; frame rate collapses.
- Receiver event log on the Chromecast (rejected by firmware).
- URL/HLS casting (catt, go-chromecast, GNOME Network Displays): 3–15 s latency.
